articles.title: Fenómeno El Niño: Ministerio de Cultura destina S/2 millones para proteger el patrimonio cultural
articles.summary: El Ministerio de Cultura destinó S/ 2 millones para implementar acciones de prevención y protección del patrimonio cultural de Lambayeque ante los posibles efectos del Fenómeno El Niño.
articles.body_text: El Ministerio de Cultura destinó S/ 2 millones para implementar acciones de prevención y protección del patrimonio cultural de Lambayeque ante los posibles efectos del Fenómeno El Niño. Así lo anunció el ministro Alberto Beingolea Delgado durante su jornada de trabajo en esta región. Explicó que los recursos estarán orientados al resguardo de museos, sitios arqueológicos y del Santuario Histórico Bosque de Pómac, así como a la ejecución de medidas preventivas para reducir los riesgos que podrían afectar estos espacios ante las lluvias intensas y otros eventos asociados al fenómeno climático. Asimismo, supervisó el Santuario Histórico Bosque de Pómac, acompañado por el director de la Dirección Desconcentrada de Cultura (DDC) de Lambayeque, Carlos Wester La Torre. Durante el recorrido, recibió información sobre las acciones preventivas y los trabajos de descolmatación del río La Leche, que contribuyen a reducir los riesgos en las zonas próximas al bosque y al patrimonio arqueológico. “El Santuario Histórico Bosque de Pómac integra valores naturales y arqueológicos. Esta visita permitirá examinar directamente los riesgos para los monumentos y reforzar la coordinación para su protección”, señaló Beingolea. El titular del sector también se reunió con el gobernador regional,Jorge Luis Pérez Flores, para abordar el proyecto de mejoramiento y ampliación de los servicios turísticos del Museo Tumbas Reales de Sipán, así como otros temas relacionados con la gestión cultural de la región. También recorrió las instalaciones del Museo Tumbas Reales de Sipán, junto con el equipo de la DDC de Lambayeque, para conocer sus condiciones actuales y revisar las necesidades relacionadas con su infraestructura, funcionamiento y proyección de inversión. Asimismo, participó en la recepción y homenaje al Señor de los Milagros, en la sede institucional de la Dirección Desconcentrada de Cultura de Lambayeque, donde la procesión congregó a numerosos fieles y recorrió las principales calles de Chiclayo. El día viernes 30 de octubre, el ministro Alberto Beingolea acompañará a la delegación encargada de evaluar los espacios previstos para las actividades del papa León XIV en Pimentel, a fin de identificar las necesidades de coordinación y articulación relacionadas con las competencias del Ministerio de Cultura. Finalmente, recorrerá el Museo Nacional de Sicán para conocer las intervenciones identificadas como Sicán 1 y Sicán 3, sus alcances y avances, así como su contribución a la conservación y funcionamiento de este espacio cultural. articles.title: Gobierno declara seis días no laborables compensables por visita del papa León XIV
articles.summary: Gobierno declara seis días no laborables compensables por visita del papa León XIV
articles.body_text: A través del Decreto Supremo N° 020-2026-TR, publicado en el diario El Peruano, el Gobierno declaró seis días no laborables compensables para los trabajadores públicos y privados por la visita del papa León XIV al Perú, próxima a realizarse del 11 al 16 de noviembre de 2026. La medida se aplicará en ocho regiones, según fechas específicas. Cabe señalar que en el sector privado, su implementación dependerá de un acuerdo entre empleadores y trabajadores. Además, las horas no trabajadas deberán recuperarse. En el caso de los servidores públicos, las horas no trabajadas deberán recuperarse dentro de los diez días inmediatos posteriores o en la oportunidad que establezca el titular de cada entidad, según sus necesidades. Según lo dispuesto, duranta la estadía del Santo Padre en nuestro país: para Lima y Callao, será los días 11, 12 y 16 de noviembre; para Cajamarca, La Libertad, Lambayeque y Piura, el 13 y 14; y para Cusco y Ucayali, el 15. La agenda del papa contempla su llegada el miércoles 11 a las 5 y 30 de la tarde para reunirse con las autoridades en Palacio de Gobierno, donde cumplirá una ceremonia de recepción y sostendrá un encuentro con la presidenta de la República. El jueves 12 estará dedicado principalmente a encuentros con representantes de la Iglesia peruana y distintos sectores de la sociedad. Para el viernes 13, el papa León XIV viajará desde Lima hacia Chiclayo durante la mañana. Una de las principales actividades será la misa en las Pampas de Pimentel, programada para las 10 y 30 de la mañana. Ya el sábado 14 visitará Santa Cruz de Succhabamba y Zaña, región Lambayeque. Asimismo, participará en una ceremonia en la Catedral de Chiclayo. El domingo 15 viajará de Cusco a Pucallpa. Primero realizará una actividad religiosa en el Parque Arqueológico de Saqsaywaman y horas más tarde una misa en la Villa Deportiva Regional de Ucayali. El lunes 16 de vuelta en Lima, continuará con las actividades finales de su visita al país. Al día siguiente, retornará a El Vaticano.

articles.title: Últimos feriados 2026 en el Perú: ¿Cuántos feriados hay en noviembre y diciembre?
articles.summary: Conoce el calendario oficial de feriados en Perú para 2026 y revisa qué días libres quedan en los últimos meses del año. Consulta las fechas de noviembre y diciembre para planificar tus viajes, actividades familiares o próximos descansos.
articles.body_text: Con el final de ciertas celebraciones del año, muchos trabajadores y estudiantes ya empiezan a revisar el calendario para conocer cuál será el siguiente descanso oficial del año. Los feriados representan una oportunidad para planificar viajes, compartir tiempo en familia o simplemente hacer una pausa en la rutina, por lo que existe un gran interés en conocer las próximas fechas establecidas por ley. Además de permitir un espacio para el descanso, estas jornadas suelen generar un importante movimiento en sectores como el turismo, el comercio, la gastronomía y el transporte, debido al incremento de personas que aprovechan los días libres para salir de la ciudad o realizar diversas actividades. Del mismo modo, muchas empresas y entidades organizan con anticipación sus operaciones para adecuarse al calendario oficial, mientras que las familias aprovechan estas fechas para programar reuniones, escapadas de fin de semana o visitas a distintos destinos del país. Por ello, conocer con anticipación cuándo será el próximo feriado resulta clave para organizar la agenda personal y laboral, evitar contratiempos y sacar el máximo provecho a los días de descanso que aún quedan en el 2026. A continuación, te contaremos todo lo que debes saber sobre esta situación. Si quieres saber cuándo será el próximo feriado y qué fechas aún quedan por disfrutar este año, aquí te contamos todos los detalles. Los feriados son fechas establecidas por ley en las que los trabajadores tienen derecho a suspender sus labores sin que ello afecte su remuneración. Durante estas jornadas, el descanso es obligatorio tanto para el sector público como para el privado, salvo en aquellas actividades que, por su naturaleza, deben continuar operando. Si un trabajador presta servicios durante un feriado y no recibe un día de descanso compensatorio, la legislación laboral establece que le corresponde una remuneración adicional por haber laborado en esa fecha, conforme a las disposiciones vigentes. A diferencia del feriado, el día no laborable no constituye un descanso obligatorio para todos los trabajadores. Generalmente, esta medida se aplica al sector público con el objetivo de extender periodos de descanso o promover actividades como el turismo interno. En el caso de las entidades públicas, las horas que no se trabajan deben recuperarse posteriormente, dentro del plazo fijado por la normativa o según lo disponga cada institución. Para el sector privado, la aplicación de un día no laborable depende de un acuerdo entre empleador y trabajadores. Si no existe consenso sobre la recuperación de las horas, será el empleador quien determine la forma en que estas deberán compensarse.

articles.title: Waymo taps Toyota to supply robotaxis for Japan and the U.K. | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Waymo will begin testing self-driving versions of Toyota's electric bZ4X vehicles in Japan next year as part of a broader partnership with the automaker.
articles.body_text: Waymo will begin testing autonomous Toyota bZ4X vehicles in Japan next year as part of a broader partnership with the automaker to provide electric vehicles for robotaxi operations in international markets, including the U.K. Under the partnership announced Friday, Toyota will manufacture the 2027 bZ4X vehicles and integrate Waymo’s self-driving system at its Takaoka factory in Japan. (The electric vehicle is now known as the BZ in the North American market) The autonomous bZ4X vehicles will initially be tested in Japan, where Waymo intends to eventually operate a robotaxi service. But the intent is to deploy these vehicles in other right-hand driving countries such as the U.K. Waymo has been testing its autonomous Jaguar I-Pace vehicles in London for months and plans to launch a robotaxi service there once it receives the necessary permits. The announcement comes 18 months after Toyota and Waymo signed a preliminary agreement to explore the development and deployment of an autonomous vehicle platform. At the time, the agreement fell into the “let’s see what happens” category, with language vague enough to leave plenty of room for interpretation. For now, the partnership looks more like a conventional vehicle supplier deal that helps Waymo fill specific regional needs while adding a new model to its robotaxi portfolio. But the partnership could go beyond robotaxis. The companies said they will continue to look at bringing Waymo’s autonomous technology to personally owned Toyota vehicles. Toyota and Waymo also announced plans to look at other future “initiatives” that would use “insights from Waymo’s real-world operations” to improve safety for other road users. What that might mean is unclear, although Hiroki Nakajima, executive vice president of Toyota and a board member, provided some clues. “This collaboration will help scale that technology and bring it to customers in Japan and beyond through Waymo’s ride-hailing service, and in parallel, Toyota will continue to explore how integrating vehicles with traffic infrastructure can make those roads safer still,” he said in a statement. articles.title: You don't need to believe in a god to get a religious exemption from using AI at work | TechCrunch
articles.summary: David Durman, a University of Kentucky administrator, recently earned a religious exemption from using AI in the workplace.
articles.body_text: Pope Leo XIV has decried AI as a threat to human dignity , but it’s not just the devoutly faithful who might worry about how AI squares with their beliefs. David Durman, a nontheistic humanist, recently secured a religious exemption from using AI in the workplace. “Humanism is a collection of beliefs about the human experience and how humans interact with the world,” Durman, a University of Kentucky administrator, told TechCrunch. It centers on “human well-being and flourishing, both individually and collectively … and implores a person to try to improve both their well-being and their flourishing as well as the others around them.” As he watched AI grow more popular in daily life, Durman sought out the American Humanist Association (AHA) — a nonprofit advancing secular humanism — to investigate how he could gain legal protections against having to use AI at work. He believes that using the technology runs counter to his beliefs. “The way we become moral actors for ourselves and for others is through the active application of our minds, and the diminishing of that [through AI use] is going to necessarily have a negative impact on our ability to do so,” he said, reflecting on how overreliance on AI might affect critical thinking. In a statement published by the AHA earlier this week, Durman wrote, “AI is interfering with people’s ability to earn a living, the environmental costs spell disaster for humanity and our planet, and its supplanting and theft of human creativity threaten elements of our culture like art and literature that make society flourish.” Humanism is not anti-religious, but it tends to appeal to people who are skeptical of a god or other supernatural power yet still seek a scientific and moral framework to ground themselves in. “Concern about AI and human dignity can run through several different faiths and traditions, whether that’s Catholic teachings, or Universalism, or Humanism, and we want Humanists or nontheists to know that they fall into these categories — that they are also protected by the law at work,” Alexandria Huiskens, staff attorney at the AHA, told TechCrunch. Durman is the first humanist to secure workplace accommodations that allow him to abstain from AI use, and one of the first people to publicly discuss their pursuit of these protections. He was inspired to seek them when he read that Erin Maus , a Unitarian Universalist and software engineer, was able to secure similar protections for herself. “For me, this was about me and my convictions,” Durman said. “I’m obviously not trying to tell people how to think or feel … But I do hope that it encourages people who have similar concerns to pursue not necessarily religious exemption, but pursue their concerns to the best of their ability where they feel is the most appropriate.” University of Kentucky spokesperson Jay Blanton told TechCrunch that the institution reviews requests for religious accommodations on an individual basis, considering the employee’s job responsibilities and the circumstances of the request. “In this case, the university determined that an accommodation could be provided while allowing the employee to continue performing the essential functions of their position,” Blanton said in a statement. “As technology and job responsibilities evolve, accommodations may be reviewed to ensure they remain reasonable and workable.” Maus’ situation is especially unusual, since it has become rare for software engineers to write code without any AI assistance. But in Durman’s administrative role, in which he supports researchers applying for grants, he has not been required to use AI at work. Like many workers across fields, some of his colleagues and leadership have recommended that employees try out these tools, so he sought to secure his exemption now, in case the suggestion becomes a mandate in the future.

articles.title: Andy Jassy says Prime Video is on track to earn 'tens of billions of dollars' | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The success of blockbuster hits like "Project Hail Mary" and "Verity" is only part of the story, Amazon's CEO says.
articles.body_text: It’s been four years since Amazon bought MGM for $8.5 billion . But coming off the blockbuster success of this year’s hit movie “Project Hail Mary,” Hollywood has become a lucrative business for the e-commerce giant. Prime Video, Amazon’s streaming service, “has emerged as a significant business with a revenue run rate in the tens of billions of dollars and is now profitable in its own right,” Amazon CEO Andy Jassy said on the quarterly earnings call on Thursday. Jassy had previously told investors in May that Prime Video was profitable , but being on track to generate tens of billions is a new detail. Amazon said its movie studio, Amazon MGM Studios, has brought in more than $1.2 billion in global box office sales so far this year, helped by hits like “Project Hail Mary” and “Verity.” “Project Hail Mary” grossed an estimated $684 million worldwide, according to The Numbers . Starring Ryan Gosling and based on Andy Weir’s novel , the film opened in theaters in March and became Amazon MGM Studios’ highest-grossing release, according to entertainment reports. (The studio also had at least one notable flop this year: “Melania.” ) Jassy also named a number of TV shows as hits, including “Carrie,” “The Summer I Turned Pretty,” “The Boys,” “Off Campus,” “Fallout,” and “Reacher.” Season 4 of “Reacher” drew 66 million viewers globally in its first 28 days, the company says, with more to come. Season 5 is filming now, and the show was picked up for a sixth season. (And if you don’t follow Alan Ritchson, the star of “Reacher,” on Threads, you are missing out on an actor who has turned a friendly-yet-witty reply into an art form.) Sports have also been a significant driver. Prime Video broadcasts NASCAR, the Masters, and UEFA Champions League soccer, but Thursday Night Football appears to be its biggest success this year. The first six games of this season have averaged 17.7 million viewers, up 16% from last year, according to Nielsen figures Amazon shared. The streaming service also attracted over 2 million viewers for its second season of the NBA on Prime, Nielsen said. When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission . articles.title: Binance pauses withdrawals as hackers suspected of stealing billions in crypto | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Some estimates say hackers stole billions in crypto from Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, during a cyberattack on Thursday.
articles.body_text: Binance has confirmed to TechCrunch that it is dealing with a security incident as users reported that funds were being drained from the crypto exchange’s wallets. The world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange said in an emailed statement to TechCrunch that it is “aware of reports of a potential security issue and are actively investigating.” “Rest assured that user funds are completely safe,” Binance said in a statement. “Our security teams are reviewing all relevant information with urgency, and we will provide updates through official Binance channels as soon as we have verified information,” the statement added. “Users should remain cautious of scams and should not trust unofficial links, messages, or requests for account information.” Binance spokesperson Ross O’Leary said that Binance has “temporarily suspended withdrawals on multiple networks following a security incident as a precautionary measure.” News of the breach comes hours after Binance founder Changpeng Zhao said in a post on X that the company likely had been hacked. Zhao, who no longer runs the company but is its largest shareholder, said that he expects users’ funds to be “fully covered” but did not provide an explanation for the claim. Financial tech giant Circle froze about $800 million in Tether as it passed through its networks, while crypto giant Tether froze about $1.56 billion related to Binance’s hack. Crypto watchers say at least $2 billion has been drained from Binance’s hot wallets, which are internet-connected cryptocurrency wallets that store crypto that are connected to the internet. By some estimates, Binance may have lost upward of $5.7 billion in crypto , though the numbers have not been confirmed and it’s possible that the theft is ongoing. It’s unclear who is behind the hack, and Binance did not say if it had received any correspondence from the hackers. If confirmed into the billions, this would likely rank as one of the largest crypto breaches in history, according to leaderboards tracking crypto thefts. In 2025, hackers stole a record $1.4 billion in crypto in a single breach from exchange Bybit, blamed on North Korean hackers. In what appears to be a separate incident earlier on Thursday, prediction market giant Polymarket briefly halted trading after it confirmed that a third-party company was compromised, which led to the company pausing withdrawals. According to security researchers, hackers stole around $2 million in user funds after compromising a piece of software developed by a company called DebugBear .

articles.title: Amazon reported booming cloud revenue but otherwise missed expectations | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The biggest ouch of the report was its negative free cash flow of $2.4 billion.
articles.body_text: Amazon reported its third-quarter earnings on Thursday and missed analysts’ expectations for both its total revenue and earnings per share. There were other murky numbers in the report that scared investors, too, including how much cash the company is burning through. But the report did have a big, bright spot: Its cloud unit, Amazon Web Services, beat revenue expectations and grew a whopping 39% compared to the year-ago quarter. But here’s the biggest ouch of the report: Free cash flow fell to a negative of $42.4 billion for the trailing 12 months — meaning the company was spending far more cash than it generated. This compares to positive free cash flow of $14.8 billion for the trailing 12 months ended September 30, 2025. The big spending was driven largely by Amazon’s investments in AI, the company said. With one quarter left in its fiscal year, Amazon reiterated that it still expects to end its 2026 with cash capital expenditures of about $220 billion. To put that in perspective, the company forecast fourth-quarter net sales of between $240 billion and $247 billion. The fourth quarter is typically a retailer’s biggest, thanks to the holiday shopping season. That means Amazon expects to spend almost as much on capital expenditures, largely for AI, over the full year as it expects to bring in from sales in the fourth quarter. articles.title: As search traffic dries up, Reddit announces it's shifting to a logged-in experience | TechCrunch
articles.summary: As AI transforms how people find information online, Reddit is rethinking its open-web roots to protect its audience and business.
articles.body_text: Reddit has long attracted millions of users to its site through Google, with many even appending the word “Reddit” to their search queries for better answers. But as search traffic dries up amid the shift to AI-powered search, Reddit is rethinking its relationship with the open internet. In its third-quarter earnings call on Thursday, the company announced it’s transitioning to a primarily “logged-in experience.” The move is designed to protect its data from AI scraping, allowing the company to instead forge lucrative licensing deals with model providers. But just as important, such a shift could help Reddit to increase its revenue even as it faces daily active user declines in its largest market, the U.S. Overall, Reddit’s global daily active users were flat quarter-over-quarter in Q3, reaching 130.3 million, while U.S. daily active users dropped from 53.2 million in Q2 to 50.7 million in Q3 and were down 2% year-over-year. The company is not alone in seeing such declines; the shift to an AI-centered web has impacted most websites and publishers by now, leading to fewer click-throughs, as AI summaries provide answers that don’t require website visits and Google’s traditional “ten blue links” have reduced relevance. (The change is now even impacting Google’s bottom line , its earnings revealed.) But at Reddit’s scale, the numbers associated with such a decline are enormous. The company said search traffic referrals dropped by more than 1 million referrals on average per week in October. It warned that if the trend continues, daily active users could decline to a low-double-digit percentage by next quarter. (To play that out: a hypothetical 10% to 12% decline could bring Reddit to roughly 115 million to 117 million daily actives, down from 130.3 million in Q3. That’s a huge drop!) At the same time, Reddit has gotten significantly better at monetizing its audience even as its growth weakens. Revenue increased 53% year-over-year to $895 million, ahead of Wall Street’s expectations of about $875 million. Net income rose 74% to $283 million. Advertising revenue grew 54% to $847 million while nonadvertising revenue, which includes its AI data-licensing business, grew 35% year-over-year to $48 million. And despite a 2% year-over-year decline in U.S. daily users, Reddit’s average revenue per daily active user in the U.S. rose 53% to $13.82. Globally, average revenue per daily active user increased 36% year-over-year to $6.87. Shifting to a logged-in experience could boost those numbers even higher because logged-in users are typically worth more to advertisers. Unlike the logged-out users who often find their way to the site via search, logged-in users provide more signals about their interests and behaviors, which helps to better target and personalize ads. Still, a change of this magnitude could be the canary in the coal mine for the open web. “I don’t know about you, but as someone whose life has been defined by the open internet, it’s a big change for me,” wrote Reddit co-founder and CEO Steve Huffman in a post published on Reddit’s site . “But I’ve come to the conclusion that this is the right decision for our platform and the right decision for our business,” he said. The company notes that the shift to the logged-in experience will not be an overnight change; it will first run tests in select markets outside the U.S. in the fourth quarter. It doesn’t yet have a timeline for when the change will be rolled out to all its users worldwide. It also acknowledged that access to a logged-out front page is important.

articles.title: The R2 SUV is already Rivian's best-selling vehicle | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Rivian is seeing strong enough sales of the new EV that it improved its guidance to Wall Street for the second time this year.
articles.body_text: Rivian’s new R2 SUV was its best-selling vehicle in the third quarter, the company said Thursday, marking an auspicious start for the all-important EV. While Rivian didn’t say exactly how many R2s it sold over the three-month period, the company is confident enough in the pace of sales that it raised its delivery guidance for Wall Street. Rivian had previously expected to deliver between 65,000 and 70,000 EVs this year. On Thursday, it bumped up that floor to 67,000. It’s the second time Rivian has raised its delivery guidance this year, and the company is now on track to break a three-year stalemate during which it struggled to ship more than 50,000 vehicles annually. The company launched the R2 just in June, but it has made a major bet on scaling production of the lower-cost SUV at a historically quick rate. The early success of the R2 is also a sign that Rivian is finding new customers despite last year’s loss of the $7,500 federal EV tax credit. The death of that tax credit, along with changes made by the Trump administration to U.S. regulations that supported the growth of EVs, has caused many major automakers to shift their attention back to internal combustion and hybrid vehicles — leaving room in the market for pure-EV companies like Tesla and Rivian. “In a U.S. automotive marketplace starved for high-quality EV choice, R2 is an attractively priced option for everyday adventures that is resonating with a broad set of consumers and we expect will be a game changer for Rivian’s long-term growth and profitability,” the company said in a letter to shareholders released Thursday. Rivian revealed earlier this month that it built 19,751 vehicles in the third quarter and delivered 19,248. That was roughly 45% more than it delivered in the same period last year and a big jump from the 12,613 vehicles built and 12,194 delivered in the second quarter of 2026. The increase was driven in large part by the company launching a second production shift at its factory in Normal, Illinois. Rivian said Thursday that the R2 was responsible for “much of the gain quarter-over-quarter,” but didn’t go into specifics. The company generated $2.2 billion in revenue in the third quarter and suffered a net loss of $913 million — down from $1.2 billion in the same period last year. Rivian launched the R2 at a starting price of just under $60,000. A more affordable “premium” trim is supposed to be available later this year that starts at $53,990. Even cheaper versions are slated for 2027, which will be available for as low as $44,990. When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission . articles.title: Bluesky blocks links to leaked DHS employee data as government seeks takedowns | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The social networking site is facing criticism for blocking access to the site, which identifies thousands of ICE agents and other employees working for Homeland Security.
articles.body_text: Following a sizable leak of personnel data about employees who work for the U.S. Department of Homeland Security, social network Bluesky is now blocking its users from accessing a nonprofit’s website that hosts the leaked dataset. Users reported that the links to nonprofit transparency collective DDoSecrets were marked as “malicious” soon after TechCrunch and other media outlets broke the news that Homeland Security had been hacked. TechCrunch reported on Wednesday that a hacker obtained over 40,000 user account records from Homeland Security’s login system, including the names and contact information, such as work-issued phone numbers and email addresses, of employees and agents working for its various agencies like Customs and Border Protection (CBP) and Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The data included information that was similar to that on an employee’s business card. DDoSecrets, which publishes leaked datasets in the public interest, also made the hacked data publicly available. Researchers who are investigating abuses by the Trump administration say that the data will be invaluable for seeking records from the government under public records laws. A spokesperson for Homeland Security told TechCrunch on Wednesday that it was “aware of a potential breach and is actively working to address the situation swiftly and effectively.” “When deciding between blocking a link and removing individual posts, we chose to block the links to avoid limiting public discussion or restricting broader access to reporting and commentary,” said Wang. In a post on Bluesky, Wang said that the company plans to change the wording on the block message. “We should have changed the wording last night. Changes incoming shortly,” said Wang. DDoSecrets co-founder and journalist Emma Best told TechCrunch that while Bluesky’s terms of service prohibit sharing home addresses and personal contact information, Best said that neither of these is in the leaked dataset. “The data contains professional contact information for government employees at a time when the public interest in that exact information has never been higher. By requiring the public to provide it for [Freedom of Information Act] requests, the government has made that exact information a crucial piece of the transparency channels they want the public to engage in,” said Best. Best told TechCrunch that a website hosting a searchable copy of the stolen data was taken down by its domain registrar, effectively knocking the website offline for now. A search site , dubbed Icepick, made by journalist maia arson crimew no longer loads as of Thursday morning. An internet record associated with the domain says it has been placed on “serverHold,” which generally means that the domain registrar locked or closed the domain for some reason. Homeland Security filed a takedown notice via a security vendor called ZeroFox, which has authority to act on the department’s behalf until 2028 to seek the removal of data from the internet. TechCrunch has seen a copy of the takedown notice for the search site, which asks that the domain registrar “stop serving the personal contact and location data of individuals who did not consent to its publication.”

articles.title: DoorDash to acquire Instacart for $17B | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The acquisition would bring two major players in on-demand delivery under one roof, combining DoorDash’s dominance in restaurant takeout with Instacart’s reach in grocery delivery.
articles.body_text: DoorDash announced on Thursday that it has agreed to acquire rival Instacart for $17 billion. The acquisition would bring two major players in on-demand delivery under one roof, combining DoorDash’s dominance in restaurant takeout with Instacart’s reach in grocery delivery. DoorDash will buy Instacart for a total value of $65 for each Instacart share, the company said. The deal has been approved by the boards of both companies. “Over the last 14 years, Instacart has transformed online grocery by helping retailers of all sizes compete and grow, and joining forces with DoorDash allows us to do even more,” said Instacart CEO Chris Rogers in a press release . “When our purpose-built grocery technology and trusted retailer and brand relationships are combined with DoorDash’s global consumer reach and logistics capabilities, we can create new opportunities for our retail and brand partners, offer an even better experience for customers and shoppers, and deliver compelling value for our shareholders.” DoorDash plans to keep Instacart’s brand, enterprise technology products, and app. The company also notes that the two brands will continue to operate as separate and independent companies until the transaction closes. DoorDash says the deal could help more grocers build out their own online ordering platforms and advertising businesses using Instacart’s technology, while grocers could also use DoorDash’s fulfillment services to handle more online orders and offer lower-cost delivery. “Grocery is one of the hardest things to get right online,” DoorDash CEO Tony Xu said in the press release. “Someone has to pick a ripe avocado, find a substitute you’d choose yourself, and get the ice cream to you before it melts. Instacart has spent years learning to do that well for grocers, while DoorDash has built a delivery network and technology that local stores rely on every day. Together, we could give stores of every size more of those tools and unlock the potential of grocery delivery. It’s still early innings, but we know that when more people shop local, more dollars stay local,” said Xu. Instacart currently has a market cap of more than $13 billion, and its stock price is up 25% for the year to date. The company likely viewed this as an opportune time to sell at a desirable price, ahead of intensifying competition in the grocery delivery market. Bloomberg previously reported that Instacart was in talks with Uber, but that the company had walked away from discussions. The deal is expected to close toward the end of 2027 or in the first half of 2028. When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission . articles.title: Upwind raises $400M after walking away from Datadog acquisition offer | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The cloud security startup raised a Series C at a $3.8B valuation, instead of selling itself for the same price.
articles.body_text: Upwind, a San Francisco startup that uses AI to secure cloud infrastructure, has raised a $400 million Series C round at a $3.8 billion valuation led by Bessemer Venture Partners, with participation from existing backers including Greylock Partners and Craft Ventures. The round comes nine months after Upwind closed its previous $250 million financing at a $1.5 billion valuation . The fresh funding, which has been in the works for months, nearly fell apart after Datadog attempted to buy the company, according to a person familiar with Upwind. Datadog is a publicly traded company that sells tools for monitoring how software runs, known as observability. It didn’t offer a premium above the $3.8 billion valuation set by venture capital investors, the person said, so Upwind decided to stay independent. Four-year-old Upwind has grown rapidly amid rising AI-driven cybersecurity threats. The startup has been adding $20 million to $30 million in annualized recurring revenue (ARR) each quarter and is projected to end the year at roughly $90 million, according to a person familiar with Upwind’s financials. That means that VCs and Datadog valued the startup at more than 40 times its forecast ARR, a common yardstick for pricing software companies. The high multiple is also well below the 80x ARR fetched by Cyera, another fast-growing cybersecurity startup, according to TechCrunch reporting from earlier this year. Cybersecurity is poised to be the third big wave of AI software that companies will pay for after AI coding tools and customer support, Theory Ventures general partner Tomasz Tunguz recently wrote in his widely read blog. By walking away from an acquisition offer, Upwind clearly believes that the company will ultimately be worth more than the $3.8 billion that Datadog was ready to pay for it. However, given how few cybersecurity companies have gone public in recent years, an eventual sale remains the most likely outcome for the startup. Upwind continues to draw acquisition interest, according to a person familiar with the company. The startup was founded by Amiram Shachar, who sold his previous company, the cloud spend management startup Spot.io, to NetApp for $450 million. Upwind calls its approach to thwarting threats “runtime” security, which means it alerts and remedies attacks and vulnerabilities in active services in real time. articles.title: Google’s new Jules AI agent will help developers fix buggy code
articles.summary: Google has announced an experimental AI-powered code agent called “Jules” that uses Gemini 2.0 to automatically fix Python and Javascript coding errors.
articles.body_text: Google has announced an experimental AI-powered code agent called “Jules” that can automatically fix coding errors for developers. Jules was introduced today alongside Gemini 2.0, and uses the updated Google AI model to create multi-step plans to address issues, modify multiple files, and prepare pull requests for Python and Javascript coding tasks in GitHub workflows. Microsoft introduced a similar experience for GitHub Copilot last year that can recognize and explain code, alongside recommending changes and fixing bugs. Jules will compete against Microsoft’s offering, and also against tools like Cursor and even Claude and ChatGPT’s coding abilities. Google’s launch of a coding-focused AI assistant is no surprise — CEO Sundar Pichai said in October that more than a quarter of all new code at the company is now generated by AI. “Jules handles bug fixes and other time-consuming tasks while you focus on what you actually want to build,” Google says in its blog post. “This effort is part of our long-term goal of building AI agents that are helpful in all domains, including coding.” Developers have full control to review and adjust the plans created by Jules, before choosing to merge the code it generates into their projects. The announcement doesn’t say that Jules will spot bugs for you, so presumably it needs to be directed to a list of issues that have already been identified to fix. Google also says that Jules is in early development and “may make mistakes,” but internal testing has shown it’s been beneficial for boosting developer productivity and providing real-time updates to help track and manage tasks. Google’s new Jules AI agent will help developers fix buggy code
articles.summary: Google has announced an experimental AI-powered code agent called “Jules” that uses Gemini 2.0 to automatically fix Python and Javascript coding errors.
articles.body_text: Google has announced an experimental AI-powered code agent called “Jules” that can automatically fix coding errors for developers. Jules was introduced today alongside Gemini 2.0, and uses the updated Google AI model to create multi-step plans to address issues, modify multiple files, and prepare pull requests for Python and Javascript coding tasks in GitHub workflows. Microsoft introduced a similar experience for GitHub Copilot last year that can recognize and explain code, alongside recommending changes and fixing bugs. Jules will compete against Microsoft’s offering, and also against tools like Cursor and even Claude and ChatGPT’s coding abilities. Google’s launch of a coding-focused AI assistant is no surprise — CEO Sundar Pichai said in October that more than a quarter of all new code at the company is now generated by AI. “Jules handles bug fixes and other time-consuming tasks while you focus on what you actually want to build,” Google says in its blog post. “This effort is part of our long-term goal of building AI agents that are helpful in all domains, including coding.” Developers have full control to review and adjust the plans created by Jules, before choosing to merge the code it generates into their projects. articles.title: The Nvidia AI antitrust investigation is ‘escalating,’ reports Bloomberg
articles.summary: Nvidia and other companies have received subpoenas indicating a Department of Justice antitrust investigation into its AI chip business is moving forward.
articles.body_text: An antitrust investigation by the Department of Justice focusing on Nvidia’s AI dominance as the hardware company of choice is escalating, reports Bloomberg. The outlet reports that Nvidia and other companies have received legally binding requests for information as its sources say regulators are investigating whether Nvidia is “making it harder to switch to other suppliers and penalizes buyers that don’t exclusively use its artificial intelligence chips.” “Nvidia wins on merit, as reflected in our benchmark results and value to customers, and customers can choose whatever solution is best for them. We have inquired with the U.S. Department of Justice and have not been subpoenaed. Nonetheless, we are happy to answer any questions regulators may have about our business,” said Nvidia spokesperson John Rizzo, as reported previously by CNBC. Earlier this summer, Nvidia had overtaken Microsoft as the world’s most valuable company, but now it trails both Microsoft and Apple. Before the subpoenas were reported on Tuesday afternoon, its share price dropped more than 9 percent, wiping out about $279 billion in market value in one day. But as Bloomberg notes, Nvidia’s stock is still up more than double this year as the AI boom has fueled sales of the company’s pricey chips, even after a report by The Information a few weeks ago saying that its upcoming Blackwell series of AI chips may be delayed “by three months or more due to design flaws.” Update, September 4th: Added Nvidia statement previously reported by CNBC.

articles.title: How AI companies are reckoning with elections
articles.summary: AI could play a prominent role in the 2024 US presidential election, and the companies behind it have each said how they plan to make sure their impact isn’t disastrous.
articles.body_text: The US is heading into its first presidential election since generative AI tools have gone mainstream. And the companies offering these tools — like Google, OpenAI, and Microsoft — have each made announcements about how they plan to handle the months leading up to it. This election season, we’ve already seen AI-generated images in ads and attempts to mislead voters with voice cloning. The potential harms from AI chatbots aren’t as visible in the public eye — yet, anyway. But chatbots are known to confidently provide made-up facts, including in responses to good-faith questions about basic voting information. In a high-stakes election, that could be disastrous. One plausible solution is to try to avoid election-related queries altogether. In December, Google announced that Gemini would simply refuse to answer election-related questions in the US, referring users to Google Search instead. Google spokesperson Christa Muldoon confirmed to The Verge via email the change is now rolling out globally. (Of course, that relies on the reliability of Google Search — something the company has been working on with an eye toward AI spam.) Muldoon said Google has “no plans” to lift these restrictions, which she said also “apply to all queries and outputs” generated by Gemini, not just text. Earlier this year, OpenAI said that ChatGPT would start referring users to CanIVote.org, generally considered one of the best online resources for local voting information. The company’s policy now forbids impersonating candidates or local governments using ChatGPT. It likewise prohibits using its tools for campaigning, lobbying, discouraging voting, or otherwise misrepresenting the voting process, under the updated rules. In a statement emailed to The Verge, Aravind Srinivas, CEO of the AI search company Perplexity, said Perplexity’s algorithms prioritize “reliable and reputable sources like news outlets” and that it always provides links so users can verify its output. In an email to The Verge, Microsoft representative Brian Gluckman says the company has rolled out updates to address concerns from a report last year about false election information provided by Copilot (formerly known as Bing). His email also pointed to the company’s blog post about combating abusive AI content as an example of the measures it’s applying, with provenance technology, bans for users who break the rules, and more. All of these companies’ responses (maybe Google’s most of all) are very different from how they’ve tended to approach elections with their other products. Google has used (and continues to use) Associated Press partnerships to bring factual election information to the top of search results and has tried to counter false claims about mail-in voting by using labels on YouTube. Other companies have made similar efforts — see Facebook’s voter registration links and Twitter’s anti-misinformation banner. Yet major events like the US presidential election seem like a real opportunity to prove whether AI chatbots are actually a useful shortcut to legitimate information. I asked a couple of Texas voting questions of some chatbots to get an idea of their usefulness. OpenAI’s ChatGPT 4 was able to correctly list the seven different forms of valid ID for voters, and it also identified that the next significant election is the primary runoff election on May 28th. Perplexity AI answered those questions correctly as well, linking multiple sources at the top. Copilot got its answers right and even did one better by telling me what my options were if I didn’t have any of the seven forms of ID. (ChatGPT also coughed up this addendum on a second try). Gemini just referred me to Google Search, which got me the right answers about ID, but when I asked for the date of next election, an out-of-date box at the top referred me to the March 5th primary. Many of the companies working on AI have made various commitments to prevent or mitigate the intentional misuse of their products. Microsoft says it will work with candidates and political parties to curtail election misinformation. The company has also started releasing what it says will be regular reports on foreign influences in key elections — its first such threat analysis came in November. Google says it will digitally watermark images created with its products using DeepMind’s SynthID. OpenAI and Microsoft have both announced that they would use the Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity’s (C2PA) digital credentials to denote AI-generated images with a CR symbol. But each company has said that these approaches aren’t enough. One way Microsoft plans to account for that is through its website that lets political candidates report deepfakes. Stability AI, which owns the Stable Diffusion image generator, updated its policies recently to ban using its product for “fraud or the creation or promotion of disinformation.” Midjourney told Reuters last week that “updates related specifically to the upcoming U.S. election are coming soon.” Its image generator performed the worst when it came to making misleading images, according to a Center for Countering Digital Hate report published last week. Meta announced in November of last year that it would require political advertisers to disclose if they used “AI or other digital techniques” to create ads published on its platforms. The company has also banned the use of its generative AI tools by political campaigns and groups. [Image: The “Seven Principle Goals” of the AI Elections accord. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/25332126/Screenshot_2024_03_12_at_11.21.50_AM.png?quality=90&strip=all] Several companies, including all of the ones above, signed an accord last month, promising to create new ways to mitigate the deceptive use of AI in elections. The companies agreed on seven “principle goals,” like research and deployment of prevention methods, giving provenance for content (such as with C2PA or SynthID-style watermarking), improving their AI detection capabilities, and collectively evaluating and learning from the effects of misleading AI-generated content. In January, two companies in Texas cloned President Biden’s voice to discourage voting in the New Hampshire primary. It won’t be the last time generative AI makes an unwanted appearance in this election cycle. As the 2024 race heats up, we’ll surely see these companies tested on the safeguards they’ve built and the commitments they’ve made. Update March 19th, 2024, 7:03PM ET: Added comment from Microsoft and additional context around Google’s Search and Associated Press partnership.

articles.title: Inside Facebook’s election war room
articles.summary: In a Menlo Park conference room, a global effort to fight misinformation comes together
articles.body_text: Information war, meet the war room. Facebook on Wednesday briefed reporters on its latest efforts to uncover nefarious uses of the platform during election season, offering a tour of the large conference room where dozens of employees are monitoring events around the clock. “We know when it comes to an elections, every moment counts,” said Samidh Chakrabarti, head of civic engagement at Facebook, who oversees the war room. “So if there are late-breaking issues we see on the platform, we need to be able to detect and respond to them in real time, as quickly as possible.” On one hand, the war room is just one of many conference rooms in MPK 20, the company’s Menlo Park, CA headquarters. But it’s larger than average, and has been stuffed with people and electronics equipment. There are desks for 24 people, and the room is ringed with 17 screens, each of which highlights a different stream of information Facebook is monitoring. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/13289699/T6B3ly8w.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] Employees look for suspicious spikes in spam and hate speech, in some cases using custom software built for the purpose. They look for efforts at voter suppression, such as falsely telling people that lines are long or that the election has been delayed. (The team recently uncovered one such hoax claiming that the Brazilian election date had been delayed a day due to protests, and swiftly removed the offending posts.) Sign up for The Interface Get The Verge’s daily newsletter about social networks and democracy the night before everyone else does. Sign up Other employees use CrowdTangle, a company acquired by Facebook that monitors the viral spread of articles across platforms, to detect which articles are trending on Facebook, Instagram, Twitter, and Reddit. All told, representatives from 20 teams have people in the war room, representing 20,000 global employees working on safety and security. The teams include threat intelligence, data science, engineering, research, operations, legal, policy, communications, and representatives from Facebook-owned WhatsApp and Instagram. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/13289701/ygMhHSnw.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] If anyone finds a problem, they escalate it to a specialist, who can then route it to the appropriate decision-maker. Facebook has also given state attorneys general and other elected officials a way to reach the war room quickly to report voter suppression and other suspicious activity. If the room is new, the work is not: Facebook teams have been working to fight misinformation in a coordinated way since 2016. The decision to bring them all together into a single room was made in the hopes that it would let them make decisions faster. “When every moment counts, then decision-making needs to be fast,” Chakrabarti sayd. “There’s no substitute for face to face, in-room interaction. so we felt [the need for] this physical war room to be able to coordinate teams.” On the day we visited, the room was decorated with a mix of American and Brazilian flags, in a nod to the next two elections that are being watched in the war room. It’s a fraught time: last week, Facebook removed 559 pages and 251 accounts in the United States for using fake identities and coordinating information campaigns. Meanwhile, Brazilian researchers today published the results of a study that examined the most-shared images in popular public WhatsApp chats and found that many of them contained misinformation: > From a sample of more than 100,000 political images that circulated in those 347 groups, we selected the 50 most widely shared. They were reviewed by Agência Lupa, which is Brazil’s leading fact-checking platform. Eight of those 50 photos and images were considered completely false; 16 were real pictures but used out of their original context or related to distorted data; four were unsubstantiated claims, not based on a trustworthy public source. This means that 56 percent of the most-shared images were misleading. Only 8 percent of the 50 most widely shared images were considered fully truthful. Facebook wouldn’t commit to keeping the war room open over forever. But with multiple elections taking place around the world each year, the company plans to keep it open for the foreseeable future. “This is going to be a constant arms race,” said Katie Harbath, Facebook’s global politics and government outreach director. “This is our new normal. Bad actors are going to get more sophisticated in what they’re doing, and we’re going to have to get more sophisticated in trying to catch them.”

articles.title: Vädjar till V – att släppa kravet: ”Offrar maktskifte”
articles.summary: Cuf-toppens krav på Andersson
articles.body_text: Cuf-ledaren Emelie Rossheim vädjar till Vänsterpartiet att släppa regeringskravet. Annars kommer den rödgröna ”soppan” inte att lösa sig, varnar hon. – Är V villiga att offra medmänsklig politik och ett maktskifte? Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Att V och C bråkar offentligt skadar den rödgröna regeringsbildningen – och det är framför allt Socialdemokraternas fel. Det tycker Emelie Rossheim, ordförande för Centerpartiets ungdomsförbund. Nu måste Magdalena Andersson klargöra om hon vill se Vänsterpartiet i regering eller inte, säger den 27-åriga Cuf-basen som väntas bli omvald i helgen. – Annars kommer vi inte att komma vidare. Emelie Rossheim kallar Vänsterpartiets regeringskrav för ”djupt oansvarigt”. – Det är utomordentligt korkat att Vänsterpartiet vill tvinga Centerpartiet att välja sida, när vi redan har uppvisat just den här enorma samarbetsviljan. För utan C blir det inget regeringsskifte. Och den här soppan kommer inte lösa sig om inte V ändrar sig. Då kommer att dröja flera år innan vi har en rödgrön majoritet. Enligt Rossheim finns det flera områden där de rödgröna kan göra gemensam sak. Hon nämner bland annat jobben, småföretagande, klimatet samt en stark röst för demokrati och mänskliga rättigheter i världen. Hon ifrågasätter hur långt Vänsterpartiet kan gå för att få ministerposter.

articles.body_text: Nu måste Socialdemokraterna ge besked om vilka de vill bilda regering med, menar Centerpartiets ledning. – Det är naturligt att Centerpartiet höjer insatserna på sin sida litegrann och markerar att regeringsbildningen är Socialdemokraternas ansvar, säger statsvetaren Andreas Johansson Heinö. Magdalena Andersson har heller inte velat berätta det för talman Andreas Norlén. – Nej, det har hon inte gjort. Hon har inte resonerat om det som efterfrågas offentligt, sa han till Expressen på torsdagseftermiddagen. Vänsterpartiet har tidigare önskat ett tydligt besked från Socialdemokraterna om att de ska få ingå i regeringen. Nu är Centerpartiet inne på samma spår. Partiets ekonomisk-politiska talesperson Martin Ådahl menar att Vänsterpartiet har ”falska förhoppningar” om att få ministerposter. – Vi tänker oss att man är lika tydlig efter valet som före med att V inte är redo för att sitta i regering. Just nu så riskerar många att kanske leva på väldigt falska förhoppningar, sa han till Svenska Dagbladet häromdagen. Nu säger Centerpartiets ledare Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist samma sak. I en kommentar om talmannens beslut att låta riksdagen rösta om henne som statsminister – trots att hon sonderade möjligheten att bilda en ”mittenregering” som skulle ledas av Magdalena Andersson – skriver hon: ”Det finns fortfarande behov av större tydlighet kring vilka regeringsalternativ inte minst Socialdemokraterna är beredda att medverka till”. Enligt uppgifter till Expressen finns en irritation mot Socialdemokraterna inom Centerpartiet. En källa i partiet beskriver situationen som ”bisarr”.

Den ena sidan förespråkar partilinjens ”öppen svenskhet”, där kultur, språk och identitet är viktigare än etnicitet. En linje som backas upp av partitoppar såsom Mattias Karlsson och Henrik Vinge och även Carl Eos vid tankesmedjan Oikos. Nu tar han dock ton och gör tydligt att det är partilinjen som gäller. ”Annars får man kliva av, eller bli avslängd” , skriver han på Expressen Debatt. articles.title: Får miljoner efter utbrott på jobbet
articles.summary: Walt blev trakasserad på jobbet som ett ”skämt”. Nu har över fyra miljoner kronor samlats in på två dagar för att stötta honom. Walt ”är helt mållös”.
articles.body_text: Walt blev trakasserad på jobbet som ett ”skämt”. Nu har över fyra miljoner kronor samlats in på två dagar för att stötta honom. Walt säger att han ”är helt mållös”, skriver Newsweek . Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Walt hade en tuff dag på jobbet i USA . Då dök det upp några personer som filmade honom medan de låtsades stjäla pengar från honom. – Mitt liv är tillräckligt svårt som det är, okej? Jag behöver inte den här skiten, säger Walt i videon. När personerna som filmade honom sade att det ”bara var ett skämt” röt Walt tillbaka: – Jag kan inte ens betala av mitt förbannade bolån. Och jag har fyra barn hemma. Så det här är inte roligt. Personerna som filmade Walt lade ut videon på Instagram, vilket de fick massiv kritik för. Men det fick också en annan konsekvens. Videon blev viral och en insamling startades för att stötta Walt. Nu har över fyra miljoner kronor samlats in till honom på två dagar. ”Walt Z från Michigan tackar innerligt och är helt mållös över hur mycket folk har brytt sig om detta”, står det på insamlingen. articles.title: Flydde i hemlighet – fick hjälp av Trump
articles.summary: Med rökridåer och avledningsmanövrar flydde Flávio Bolsonaro från Brasilien. Till sin hjälp hade han bland andra Donald Trumps allierade och Argentinas president Javier Milei.
articles.body_text: Med rökridåer och avledningsmanövrar flydde Flávio Bolsonaro från Brasilien. Till sin hjälp hade han bland andra Donald Trumps allierade och Argentinas president Javier Milei. Wall Street Journal har kartlagt den besegrade presidentkandidatens dramatiska flykt till USA. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Operationen tog form i måndags, mindre än ett dygn efter förlusten mot Lula da Silva. Bolsonaros allierade befarade att han skulle gripas om han stannade kvar i landet. Några timmar tidigare hade landets högsta domstol belagt honom med reseförbud och beordrat honom att lämna ifrån sig sina pass. Beslutet fattades mot bakgrund av brottsutredningar om penningtvätt och korruption som inleddes 2019 mot den dåvarande presidentsonen. Samma kväll lämnade Bolsonaro sitt hem i Brasília. Han färdades i en konvoj med fyra mörka bilar som snart skingrades åt olika håll. Manövern gjorde det svårt för både journalister och myndigheter att avgöra vilken bil han satt i. Redan på tisdagen började uppgifter sippra ut om att presidentkandidaten befann sig i Florida. Men även det var en del av Bolsonaros teams vilseledningsmanöver. I själva verket var han fortfarande kvar i Brasilien . Först sent på tisdagskvällen tog han sig över gränsen till Argentina tillsammans med sin fru och parets två döttrar. På flygplatsen i Puerto Iguazú väntade ett chartrat privatplan. Strax efter midnatt lyfte det mot USA, med en mellanlandning i Ecuador. På onsdagsmorgonen landade familjen i Miami. Där möttes de av uniformerade poliser som höll upp paraplyer för att skymma dem från fotograferna. Familjen fördes sedan snabbt till en väntande bil och lämnade flygplatsen under poliseskort.

articles.title: Stal 62 miljarder – på 20 minuter
articles.summary: En hackerattack har genomförts mot kryptobörsen Binance. 62 miljarder kronor misstänks ha stulits på 20 minuter. Det beskrivs som ”största kuppen någonsin”.
articles.body_text: En omfattande hackerattack har genomförts mot kryptobörsen Binance. 62 miljarder kronor misstänks ha stulits – på 20 minuter. Det beskrivs som ”största kuppen någonsin” av Sky News och Wall Street Journal . Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Binance, en av världens största kryptobörser, uppgav natten mot fredagen att man utreder en cyberattack. Kryptovaluta värd mer än 20 miljarder kronor har därför spärrats på plattformen. ”Det ser ut som en hackerattack mot Binance”, skriver Binances grundare Changpeng Zhao på X. 62 miljarder kronor misstänks ha stulits, enligt kryptoanalysföretaget TRM Labs. – Detta är extraordinärt med tanke på dess storlek, säger Ari Redbord, policychef på TRM Labs, till Sky News. Stölden ska ha begåtts av nordkoreanska hackare – och den ska bara ha tagit 20 minuter. Wall Street Journal och Sky News beskriver det som ”största kuppen någonsin”. Binance påstod initialt att användarnas medel är ”helt säkra” och att deras säkerhetsteam ”brådskande granskar all relevant information”. Crypto Watchdogs vd Chapin Fay varnade för att frysning av tillgångar inte garanterar att stulna medel kommer att återfås.
